2240.resolution: Real ambiguity (both), fixed: 'sine qua' was attached to 'volition'; now 'begin from faith of this kind, without which no good work can exist', keeping the feminine antecedent with faith as both models read it; 'heretics for example' is now 'such as heretics' ('quales sunt haeretici'). Rejected: 'we give to God speaking in his word' = 'Deo in verbo suo loquenti adhibemus' (the faith we bring to God who speaks). Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi): rejected; 'we give to God' = 'adhibemus' (repeat); 'They will have ... begin' = 'incipere volunt'; 'no good work can exist' = 'impossibile est esse'; result 'sint' rendered as fact.

2241.resolution: Partly accepted: 'where freedom from sin begins' is now 'from which' ('unde'); the accusative-and-infinitive report is now marked ('on this view', 'he holds'). Rejected: 'choice is not free' = 'non sit ei liberum' ('ei' is the 'arbitrium' just named); 'cannot undo' renders 'insolubili'; 'nor even one' and 'not even in a single work' = 'nec quidem' and 'nec in uno quidem'; 'wholly without sin' = 'sine omni peccato'; 'temptation to sin' = 'peccati tentationem'. Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi): one point accepted: 'sed' restored ('not only cannot live wholly without sin ..., but every act of his ... is a sin'). Rejected: 'ei' again (= arbitrium); 'the grace of faith' supplies the 'gratia' understood with 'fidei'; 'nec ... quidem' is rendered 'not even'. Round 3 (kimi): all rejected, no change. The subject of 'fecerit', 'liberetur', 'ei', 'meditatur' and 'se verterit' is 'arbitrium' (choice), named in 'arbitrium post lapsum hominis ita captivum esse' and continued through the passage; 'not even morally good' = 'neque sit moraliter bonum' after 'non tantum'; the reported construction is marked ('on this view', 'he holds'); 'wholly without sin' = 'sine omni peccato'.

2242.resolution: Two points accepted: 'with which the Christian religion begins' is now 'from which' ('a qua'); 'in detail' is now 'specifically' ('speciatim'). Rejected: 'sets out to prove' = 'probare aggreditur'. Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi): rejected; 'following Augustine' = 'juxta Augustinum'; 'vero' is a connective.

The 'dropped clause' is present ('So to do good by loving the righteousness of the law is nothing other than to do good by loving God himself with the charity of the Holy Spirit'); 'righteousness is loved by charity alone' = 'nec illa, nisi sola charitate diligitur'; 'in Augustine's own words' = 'verbis ipsis Augustini'; 'because it is faith that obtains' carries 'ideo ... quia ipsa est quae ... impetrat'; 'that there is no good work' renders the accusative and infinitive. Checked clause by clause against the Latin; the English keeps the sense, agents, negations and modality of the source.

2244.resolution: Two small points accepted: 'stain' is now 'contamination' ('contaminatione'); 'Unde quoque' is now 'Hence also'. 2245.resolution: Partly accepted: 'accept' is now 'approve' ('minime probat'); 'imo nec ... notitiam & fidem' is now 'indeed does not even have knowledge of and faith in the one true God'; 'An example' is now 'As when' ('Ut quum'). 'For it is absolutely necessary' renders causal 'Cum ... necesse sit'; 'come to rest' = 'sistat se'; 'whatever that creature is supposed to be' = 'qualiscunque tandem ea supponatur'. 2249.resolution: One point accepted: 'cannot excuse themselves' is now 'cannot be excused' ('excusari possunt'). Rejected: 'the one who seems to act from virtue' = 'qui ex virtute agere videtur'. Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi): rejected; the model concedes the sense ('same sense').

2250.resolution: One point accepted: 'though it was thought to be a virtue' is now 'which had been thought to be a virtue' ('quae virtus esse putabatur'). Rejected: the 'invented clause' is the quotation 'Qui non levat oculos suos ad Deum', which is in the Latin (the model misaligned it with 'Cum enim'); 'cannot seek it without pleasing himself by it, nor seek it without wishing to please himself by it' = 'impossibile est, ut eam vel appetens non inde sibi placeat, vel non inde sibi placere volens appetat'. Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi): rejected; the same misalignment of the 'Qui non levat oculos' quotation with 'Cum enim'; 'cannot ... without' is the same logic as 'impossibile est ut ... non'; 'the philosophers' virtue' = 'Philosophicae virtutis'.

'referred to God, to be possessed in eternal life' = 'ad Deum in aeterna vita possidendum'; 'it also follows' = 'inde quoque consequens est'; 'divide ... in vain' = 'frustra ... distinguere'; 'and so' = 'ac proinde'. 2252.resolution: Real error (glm), fixed: conditional 'si non referatur' had been rendered as causal 'since'; now 'and if it is not so referred it is a sin by the very fact that its end is not right'. Julian's division now keeps 'per quos ... boni sumus': 'some through which we are good barrenly and others through which we are good fruitfully, that is, those which ... either help toward obtaining eternal life or do not'. 'faith in and love of' is now 'faith and love of' ('ex fide atque dilectione'). Rejected: kimi's 'invented' quotation is in the Latin (part-split artifact); 'in its own way meritorious' keeps 'suo modo'. Re-reviewed after the fix. 2253.resolution: Reworded: 'not yet justified and have not obtained' is now 'have not yet been justified and obtained the forgiveness of their sins', so the single 'nondum' governs both participles as in the Latin (they share 'sunt'); sinners in mortal sin have not obtained remission, as Le Blanc says. A note explains the scope. 'Session 6, canon 7' = 'Canone septimo Sessionis sextae'. Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi): rejected; citation order and 'pronounces anathema' for 'anathema dicit'; glm now passes.
